title: When Better Codebooks Are Not Enough: Predictive Performance and Rule Adherence in LLM Political Event Coding
abstract: arXiv:2606.06781v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: High accuracy alone does not establish whether an LLM follows a codebook. This matters because many social-science studies rely on expert-written codebooks to turn text into structured data. We study this problem in political event coding, a source-target relation classification task in which a model identifies the action that one actor directs toward another under detailed coding rules. We test whether expert codebooks become more effective when presented to LLMs through clearer definitions, examples, retrieved context, and rules for difficult cases. We then examine how model predictions respond to controlled changes in label names, codebook order, and label-definition mappings. translated_title: 当更好的编码手册仍不足够：大语言模型政治事件编码中的预测性能与规则遵循
translated_abstract: 高准确率本身并不能证明大语言模型是否遵循编码手册。这一点非常重要，因为许多社会科学研究依赖专家编写的编码手册将文本转化为结构化数据。我们在政治事件编码中研究这一问题，这是一个“来源—目标”关系分类任务，模型需要在详细的编码规则下识别一个行为者针对另一个行为者所采取的行动。我们测试了当专家编码手册通过更清晰的定义、示例、检索到的上下文以及针对困难案例的规则呈现给大语言模型时是否会变得更有效。随后，我们考察了模型预测如何响应标签名称、编码手册条目顺序以及标签—定义映射的受控变化。更清晰的编码手册改进了细粒度分类：在四个开源大语言模型上，根层级的平均宏F1从仅使用标签名称时的0.457提升至使用增强指导后的0.633。然而，调换增强编码手册中条目的顺序会导致21.2%的（预测发生变化）……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究发现，在政治事件编码任务中，更清晰的编码手册能显著提升大语言模型的细粒度分类性能（根层级宏F1从0.457升至0.633），但模型预测对条目顺序等表面变化高度敏感，表明准确率的提升并不等于模型真正遵循了编码规则。
en_tdlr: This study finds that clearer codebooks substantially improve LLM fine-grained classification in political event coding (root-level macro-F1 rising from 0.457 to 0.633), yet predictions remain highly sensitive to superficial changes such as entry order, showing that higher accuracy does not imply genuine adherence to coding rules.
